## 型

### InvalidUrl

```emela
error InvalidUrl(url: String)
```

The URL cannot be read as a URL.

- `url: String`

### ConnectionFailed

```emela
error ConnectionFailed(url: String, message: String)
```

No response was received (name resolution, connection, TLS, too many redirects). `message` says why.

- `url: String`
- `message: String`

### ResponseNotText

```emela
error ResponseNotText(url: String)
```

The response body is not valid UTF-8.

- `url: String`

### Http

```emela
effect Http
```

Sends requests. 4xx and 5xx are responses, not failures; fail only when no response is received.

- `suspend fn send(request: Request) -> Response fails InvalidUrl | ConnectionFailed | ResponseNotText`

  Sends `request` and returns its response.

### SystemHttp

```emela
handler SystemHttp: Http
uses { Async }
```

The host's HTTP client (JS `fetch`). It follows redirects, keeps no cookies and ignores the
proxy environment variables. Interrupting the fiber waiting on `send` aborts the request
(`[ext.call]`).

### TestServer

```emela
type TestServer(respond: fn(Request, Int) -> Option[Response], sent: List[Request])
```

The server that TestHttp sends to. `respond` gets the request and how many requests were sent
before it (from 0), and returns the response, or `None` for ConnectionFailed. `sent` holds the
sent requests in order.

- `respond: fn(Request, Int) -> Option[Response]`
- `sent: List[Request]`

### TestHttp

```emela
handler TestHttp: Http
uses { State[TestServer] }
```

The test handler. The server is `State[TestServer]`, so use it inside `State.run`:

```emela
server = TestServer(respond: |req, n| Some(Response.new(200, "ok")), sent: [])
(res, after) = State.run(server, || with TestHttp { Http.get("https://example.com") })
```

`send` adds the request to `sent` and resumes at once. It never fails with InvalidUrl or
ResponseNotText.

### Incoming

```emela
type Incoming
```

The request as the host handed it over (JS: a Fetch API Request). Used only when writing an
export by hand.

### Outgoing

```emela
type Outgoing
```

The response for the host to send (JS: a Fetch API Response).

## 値

### get

```emela
fn get(url: String) -> Response fails InvalidUrl | ConnectionFailed | ResponseNotText uses { Http }
```

Sends a GET request to `url`.

### post

```emela
fn post(url: String, body: String) -> Response fails InvalidUrl | ConnectionFailed | ResponseNotText uses { Http }
```

Sends a POST request to `url` with `body`.

### request

```emela
fn request(method: Method, url: String) -> Request
```

A request with no headers and an empty body.

### add_header

```emela
fn add_header(req: Request, name: String, value: String) -> Request
```

Adds a header after the ones already in `req`.

### header

```emela
fn header(res: Response, name: String) -> Option[String]
```

The first value of the header `name`, compared without case.

### headers

```emela
fn headers(res: Response, name: String) -> List[String]
```

All values of the header `name` in order, compared without case.

### encode_query

```emela
fn encode_query(pairs: List[(String, String)]) -> String
```

The query string of `pairs`, each part percent-encoded (`q=%E6%9D%B1&page=2`).

### require_ok

```emela
fn require_ok(res: Response) -> Response fails UnexpectedStatus
```

`res` if its status is 2xx, otherwise fails with UnexpectedStatus.

### response

```emela
fn response(status: Int, body: String) -> Response
```

A response with no headers.

### serve

```emela
fn serve[E, F](app: fn(Request) -> Response fails E uses { Async, ProcessHost, Spawn[F, Async] }, incoming: Incoming) -> Outgoing uses { Async, ProcessHost }
```

The entry of an HTTP service (`[lib.http-service]`): `@entry(Http.serve)` on `app` makes the
host call `app` once for each request, and each call is one launch. The request is read whole
before `app` runs. A method not in `Method` is answered with 405, and a body that is not UTF-8
or a path or query with a malformed `%` with 400, without calling `app`. When `app` fails, has
a defect or returns a response the host cannot send, the cause is written to standard error as
one line and the response is 500; the cause is never in the response. An HTTP service runs in
a process, so `app` is given ProcessHost (`[effect.host]`) and can write `with Process { ... }`.

`app` is called inside a `Task.Background` that provides Spawn by name. The response goes to
the host as soon as `app` returns, and the launch ends when the release of that background has
waited for the tasks `app` started. A task that ends with an error or a defect writes its cause
to standard error as one line.
